string-array.name: help_rpm
string-array.item: Engine speed.
600–900 rpm at warm idle on most petrol engines. Higher after a cold start, coming down as the engine warms up.
If the idle hunts on a warm engine, look at per-cylinder misfires and fuel trims on the \"Fuel\" tab.

string-array.name: help_speed
string-array.item: Vehicle speed as the engine ECU sees it.
The speedometer usually reads a little high. The easy check is GPS speed at a steady pace.
If it\'s always off from GPS, the tires are probably a different size. Then the mileage and L/100km are off too.

string-array.name: help_coolant
string-array.item: Coolant temperature.
Usually 85–105 °C on a warm engine, and steady. The fan comes on near the top of that range.
Slow to warm up: possibly a thermostat stuck open (often with code P0128). Keeps climbing: check the coolant level, fans and water pump.

string-array.name: help_load
string-array.item: Calculated load: how much air the engine is drawing in now, relative to the maximum.
Usually 20–40 % at warm idle, close to 100 % at full throttle. Lower at full throttle up in the mountains, where the air is thin.
If full throttle at the same rpm gives less than it used to, the engine is short of air: air filter, MAF, throttle.

string-array.name: help_throttle
string-array.item: Throttle position. The ECU opens the throttle following the pedal.
A closed throttle usually reads 10–20 %, and wide open doesn\'t reach 100 %. That\'s just how it\'s measured.
Jumps while the pedal is still, or the car went into limp mode: the throttle body or its sensors (codes P2135, P2101).

string-array.name: help_pedal
string-array.item: Accelerator pedal position, sensor D. The pedal has two sensors, D and E, and the ECU keeps cross-checking them.
A released pedal usually reads 10–20 %, floored about 80 %.
Jumps while your foot is still: the pedal assembly or its connector (code P2138). Sensor E is on the \"All data\" tab and should move together with D.

string-array.name: help_timing
string-array.item: Ignition advance in degrees before TDC. The ECU pulls it back when it hears knock.
Usually 5–20° at idle, more when cruising, less at full throttle.
Look at knock retard on the \"Fuel\" tab. Frequent retard means the engine is knocking: bad fuel or overheating.

string-array.name: help_maf
string-array.item: Air flow from the MAF sensor, in grams per second. The ECU uses it to work out how much fuel to inject.
At warm idle roughly 1–1.5 g/s per liter of engine size. Worth noting your own value to compare against later.
Lower than usual at idle, with fuel trims gone positive: a dirty MAF or an air leak after it.

string-array.name: help_map
string-array.item: Intake manifold pressure (absolute).
Ignition on, engine off: equal to atmospheric. Usually 25–40 kPa at warm idle, almost atmospheric at full throttle. A turbo engine goes above atmospheric under boost.
Noticeably higher than usual at warm idle: an air leak, valve timing off, or low compression.

string-array.name: help_iat
string-array.item: Intake air temperature.
A little above the outside temperature while driving. Much higher in traffic and after parking with a hot engine, drops quickly once moving.
−40 °C almost always means an open sensor circuit.

string-array.name: help_runtime
string-array.item: Seconds since the engine was started.
Went back to zero while driving: the engine stalled or the ECU rebooted.
